summary: Terminal UI demo for SOX Protocol — the artefact that gets embedded in the README and shown in the launch narrative. Built with Textual on top of the existing Python sox_protocol client. Owns the primitive coverage slots that benefit from live, fast-redrawing visuals: dm/<sorted-pair> channel creation via /dm command, channels_heartbeat liveness shown in the agent_roster pane, and the choreographed two-agent demo recording. Coverage divides cleanly with chat-webapp (which owns replay scrubber + group sidebar) and reference-agent (which owns deeply-annotated single-agent lifecycle).

panes.name: channel_list
panes.purpose: all subscribed channels grouped by prefix (group/, dm/, sox/, free-form); active channel highlighted; unread badge per channel

panes.name: message_feed
panes.purpose: scrolling list of messages for the active channel; each bubble shows seq:N inline, sender, body.subject, and a thread arrow when reply_to is set

panes.name: agent_roster
panes.purpose: PRIMITIVE COVERAGE: presence/heartbeat. Live presence panel subscribed to sox/presence; coloured dot per agent (green online, yellow busy, grey stale, dim offline); animates the online→busy transition the demo script triggers

panes.name: compose_bar
panes.purpose: input field with prompt; supports slash-commands enumerated below

interactions: /reply <message_id>  — sets reply_to for the next send (covers reply_to in TUI)
/dm <agent-id>       — opens dm/<sorted-pair> channel via SDK canonical name helper (PRIMITIVE COVERAGE: dms)
/ack <message_id> [reason]  — calls channels_ack tool with status=done (or nack if reason given) — proves ACK does NOT appear in feed
/heartbeat <online|busy|offline>  — manual heartbeat trigger for the demo

choreography.action: agent A bootstraps, subscribes to #general, channels_heartbeat(online) — roster shows A green
agent B bootstraps similarly — roster shows A,B green
agent A sends 'Which schema version?' to #general — feed shows seq:1 from A
agent B reads the message; channels_ack(received), then channels_ack(processing) — neither appears in feed (proof point)
agent B replies 'v3' with reply_to=msg-1 — feed shows seq:2 from B with thread arrow pointing to seq:1
agent A channels_ack(done) on the reply — NOT visible in feed
agent A opens DM: /dm agent-b → channel becomes dm/agent-a~agent-b (lex-sorted) — sidebar gains a DM section entry
agent A sends 'thanks' on the DM — feed shows seq:1 (independent counter on the new DM channel)
agent B channels_heartbeat(busy) — roster transitions B's dot from green→yellow
agent B channels_heartbeat(online) — back to green
agent B graceful_stop: heartbeat(offline) then unsubscribe — roster fades B to dim

recording_strategy.tool: vhs (Charm) — chosen over asciinema-only because vhs renders deterministically from a .tape script (frame-accurate, no human typing variability) and emits both .gif and .cast in one pass; asciinema alone requires manual recording which fails the 'running it twice produces the same recording' constraint
recording_strategy.post_process: vhs runs demo.tape → emits demo.gif directly; demo.cast is captured by piping demo.py through asciinema rec inside the tape; both committed
recording_strategy.rationale: Determinism is the hard constraint. The .tape script encodes wall-clock waits matching demo.py choreography; running `vhs demo.tape` twice produces byte-identical artefacts (subject to vhs version pin). Total artefact size budget: ≤5MB across both files; current estimate ~2MB for a 45s 80x24 GIF at 10fps.

test_cases: slash-command parser maps to SDK calls
/ack does not insert into feed state
watch_loop pumps store on each recv message
demo.py runs to completion in ≤60s without input
running demo.py twice produces identical message-id sequences (modulo timestamps) — choreography is deterministic

risks.mitigation: use Textual's Pilot harness for headless snapshot testing; render-only branches excluded from coverage with documented justification in conftest.py

risks.risk: Demo timing drift if agent processing varies
risks.mitigation: demo.py uses asyncio.sleep at wall-clock anchors driven by an OrchestratorClock, not by 'wait for next event' — choreography is time-driven, not state-driven, ensuring reproducibility
vhs at 80x24 @ 10fps for 45s is ~2MB; budget includes 2x headroom; CI asserts size; fall back to lower fps or shorter shot if exceeded

risks.risk: Choreography overlaps webapp/reference-agent coverage and creates maintenance duplication
risks.mitigation: primitives_demonstrated is explicitly scoped to live-display primitives (presence/dm/seq/thread visualisation/ack-NOT-in-feed proof); replay scrubber and group sidebar are intentionally NOT in the TUI demo — they live in chat-webapp; deeply-annotated lifecycle code lives in reference-agent

risks.risk: ACK-not-in-feed proof point is invisible to a viewer
risks.mitigation: demo.py prints a side-channel banner overlay 'ACK sent (control-plane, not in history)' at t=5/9/13 so viewers see the negative space
